title: Frontiers: Can an Artificial Intelligence Algorithm Mitigate Racial Economic Inequality? An Analysis in the Context of Airbnb
near_miss_reason: The design is a staggered binary adoption (hosts adopt Smart Pricing in 21 different months, 7,237 never-adopters in the shipped sample) with property fixed effects, but every reported column (Table 2 and Table 3) adds eight time-varying property-level controls and inverse-probability-of-treatment weights from a logit on baseline covariates (IPW is excluded under PROTOCOL 5b); Table 3 further adds smart x race interactions. The time fixed effects are city x year and city x month-of-year rather than city x year-month. No unweighted, control-free TWFE column is reported.
design_notes: Property-month panel of Airbnb listings (Airbnb_Pricing_Data.dta: 211,853 rows, 9,396 properties, periods 19-44 = Jul 2015-Aug 2017; Smart Pricing launched in period 23 = Nov 2015). treat = ever adopted (2,118 properties in the 80% sample); AdoptMonth = first month using Smart Pricing (values 24-44, mode 29); smart = contemporaneous usage, which is switched off in 9,083 of 24,424 post-adoption treated property-months. Main regressions: xtreg Y smart controls i.city_year i.city_month [pw=iweight], fe vce(cluster PropertyID). Weights: logit of treat on time-invariant property/host/neighbourhood covariates and period-23 values of time-varying covariates, iweight = 1/p for adopters and 1/(1-p) for non-adopters. Table 3 interacts smart with host race (RaceInd). Table S9 adds pre-adoption leads. Tables S5-S6 / Figures S2-S3 are tesensitivity (conditional c-dependence) bounds on a cross-sectional ATE, not DiD.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: AdoptMonth takes 21 distinct values (24-44) among 2,118 ever-adopting properties in the 80% sample (hist AdoptMonth is Figure 1).

data_files: Replication Code and Data/Airbnb_Pricing_Data.dta (56 MB, Stata; 80% random subsample of the property-month panel, disguised PropertyID)
data_files_note: README: 'We provide a random subsample of the data (80%) ... point estimates differ, but the main findings hold.' PropertyID disguised under NDA but consistent within property. Per PROTOCOL 5b a random subsample counts as original data with a flag (data_provenance = real_random_subsample_80pct). All regression variables are present.
priority_note: Not eligible as reported (near-miss). A control-free, unweighted TWFE/CSA re-estimation on the shipped 80% sample would be feasible for a near-miss sensitivity exercise, with the caveat that smart switches off after adoption (drop post-adoption months with smart==0 per PROTOCOL 5b).
screener_notes: Screened from package only. Adoption-month distribution, never-treated count and the switching-off share were computed from Airbnb_Pricing_Data.dta with pandas. Note city_month = group(CityInd, month) uses calendar month-of-year, not year-month, so the time FE are seasonal + annual rather than full monthly.
eligible_design_note: set to false Nov 1 ~22:05 (coding rule, PROTOCOL 5b): near-miss with no main-text specification satisfying every design rule
